Priya M: FYI support escalation from BetaCustomer: sudden jump in p95/p99 on dedicated pool rw-us-west-1-gpu-b starting ~02:40 UTC. They see slow tails (~2.8s) and occasional 500 errors.
Leo H: Any model/variant info?
Priya M: 70B-int8-optimized, rolling with long-conversation workloads. Ticket says KV size per conversation hit ~3GB for a handful of sessions.
Tom B: Do we have node-level OOMs or just allocation failures?
Priya M: Customer logs show allocation failures followed by long stall while runtime tries retries/slow-paths. Not full kernel kill every time, but lots of cudaMallocAsync fallback logs.
Priya M: snippet from host gpu-17 at 02:39:57:
```
[02:39:57] runtime: cudaMallocAsync failed: not enough memory
[02:39:57] runtime: attempting memory pooling fallback
[02:40:03] runtime: large allocation waited 4500ms -> request timed out
[02:40:04] api: 500 internal error - allocation failure
```
Leo H: Noted. If cudaMallocAsync fallback is used frequently it increases latencies massively. Also fragmentation could mean free memory exists but not large contiguous blocks.
Tom B: Do we track per-session KV sizes in our metrics?
Priya M: We have internal counters but not surfaced to Console for customers. The beta customer included a dump showing 6 sessions each >2.5GB KV.
ops-bot: Alert created: high-p99-latency detected on pool rw-us-west-1-gpu-b (threshold 1500ms). Incident ID: INC-2241.
Priya M: Short-term mitigation ideas: 1) cap per-session KV bytes 2) reject extra-large requests with 413 3) restart long-lived model processes to defrag 4) move this customer's workload to a pool with larger GPU per-node memory.
Leo H: Which of these can we do quickly without customer impact? Restart is quick but disruptive. Config cap per-session and reject new appends beyond cap is safer.
Tom B: We can implement a per-session reject policy keyed by session_id — return a structured error asking to truncate conversation. Low-risk config toggle.
Priya M: Customer prefers non-disruptive. Can we soft-throttle append calls once session KV > X?
Leo H: Yes, implement soft-throttle + warning header for client. But the current client libs maybe not handling that gracefully. We'll add a clear error code and docs.
Priya M: Repro done by infra: spin up 8 long sessions with repeated embed+append -> within 20-30 minutes the allocator starts returning failed async allocations. Repro steps below.
```
Repro (48GB-A100 dev box):
1) run server with --enable-cuda-malloc-async=true --kv-global-max=0
2) create 8 sessions, for i in 1..8: post 40k tokens via /chat/append
3) every 15s call /embed for each session
4) watch `nvidia-smi` and runtime logs
Expected: by ~25 min, cudaMallocAsync starts failing for large contiguous allocations and p99 spikes
```
Tom B: For mid-term: enable compacting GC for KV (free unused slabs), consider migrating to cuMemPool / cudaMallocAsync tuned thresholds, and add a background compaction run during low load. Also consider reserving a small contiguous pool for attention scratch allocs.
Leo H: The 'reserve contiguous pool' idea: we pre-alloc a few hundred MB per model process for transient large allocations and recycle it after use. That reduces hard failures but increases baseline mem usage. Tradeoffs.
priya m: Customer asked for ETA on fix and whether we can prevent recurrence.
Tom B: Plan: immediate config change to set per-session kv cap=1GB and enable soft-throttle on append >85% of cap; flip for pool rw-us-west-1-gpu-b. Also add an automated restart policy for processes that hit repeated allocation failures (n failures within t). I'll prototype allocator tuning in a branch.
deploy-bot: Deploy request queued: set kv.session_max_bytes=1073741824 and kv.soft_throttle_threshold=0.85 for pool rw-us-west-1-gpu-b.
Leo H: Canary rollout at 10% for 3 minutes, monitor p95/p99 and allocation error rate.
oncall: Can someone own customer comms?
Priya M: I'll update BetaCustomer and give them the mitigation timeline.
Tom B: Observability gaps: we need per-session contiguous-free-block metric, and a histogram of allocation sizes that fail. Add to backlog.
Leo H: Also add a Console alert to surface when a pool's alloc-fail-rate > X per minute.
Priya M: After canary started, canary hosts showed drop in allocation-fail-rate and p99 down from ~2.8s to ~980ms. Increasing rollout to 50%.
ops-bot: Canary metrics: allocation_fail_rate reduced by 78% on canary nodes.
Tom B: Postmortem action items: - surface per-session KV usage in Console - default kv.session_max_bytes for dedicated pools - implement background KV compaction + compaction API - evaluate cuMemPool vs cudaMallocAsync settings across model sizes - implement pre-reserved contiguous buffer for attention ops (opt-in)
Leo H: I'll create the RFC for allocator/reservation strategies. Tom, please attach repro artifacts to your PR.
Priya M: Customer reported latency improved after config change; they'll monitor and report if they see edge cases. Closing incident once 50% rollout completes and no regressions in 2 hours.
Tom B: Note: need to add tests that simulate fragmentation (frequent small frees + some large allocs) in CI to prevent regressions.
Priya M: Thanks all. I'll file the post-incident ticket and include recommended default caps. :thumbsup:
oncall: Incident INC-2241 updated to RESOLVED (mitigation: kv caps + soft-throttle).
